abstract_core: In an internally pre-specified 2025 day-ahead test, adding extracted news labels to the numerical reference changed its mean absolute error by +0.18% (+0.0928 AUD/MWh; one-sided Diebold–Mariano p = 0.61).
In the same year, price-only LEAR, added after that test, had a 21.3% lower mean absolute error than the numerical reference (39.73 against 50.51 AUD/MWh).

For day-ahead news, no structured representation improved on the article activity reference (the label-count representation 11.412% [1.220, 26.787], Holm-adjusted p = 0.086, fragile (one-day interval); the structured-attribute embedding 1.171% [-3.298, 5.625], Holm-adjusted p = 0.558, not fully checked; family-adjusted 97.5% intervals); improvements larger than 3.298% of the reference error were excluded at the family-adjusted one-sided 1.25% level, below the 3.8% smallest effect size of interest.

For market notices, the event-state representation improved on the notice activity reference by 0.303% of the reference error (0.0287 AUD/MWh; family-adjusted 98.3% interval [-0.403, -0.201]%, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001); it was robust and an increment over the notice activity reference only, not shown to be LLM-specific; its interval lies wholly below the 0.5% historical-effect reference; it persisted when each forecast was averaged with the reference augmented with five-minute pre-dispatch prices.

For market notices, the message, failure and fuel-group counts improved on the notice activity reference by 0.284% of the reference error (0.0269 AUD/MWh; family-adjusted 98.3% interval [-0.398, -0.165]%, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001); it was fragile (three-seed mean) and an increment over the notice activity reference only, not shown to be LLM-specific; its interval lies wholly below the 0.5% historical-effect reference; it persisted when each forecast was averaged with the reference augmented with five-minute pre-dispatch prices.

For market notices, the structured-attribute notice embedding improved on the notice activity reference by 0.747% of the reference error (0.0706 AUD/MWh; family-adjusted 98.3% interval [-1.019, -0.473]%, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001); it was robust and an increment over the notice activity reference only, not shown to be LLM-specific; its point estimate exceeds the 0.5% historical-effect reference but its interval straddles it; it persisted when each forecast was averaged with the reference augmented with five-minute pre-dispatch prices.

These readings are relative to the pre-specified learner and information set: the primary news reference uses no operator forecasts and the primary notice reference uses no five-minute pre-dispatch prices.

fixed_sentences.A3C8: Content controls exist only for the two structured-attribute embeddings. For the label-count representation, the event-state representation and the message, failure and fuel-group counts, activity-matched reassignment or 28-day shifting would require new features, so their increments are described relative to activity only and compared with cheap-text representations of the same documents.
fixed_sentences.A3D5: The transferred 3.8% value is not informative for the notice task, whose expected bounds are an order of magnitude smaller; the notice reading is compared with the 0.5% historical-effect reference, with the earlier notice text effects and with the minimum detectable effect.
fixed_sentences.A3P1: A planted-signal check on pre-confirmation windows of the same size added to the activity reference a column equal to the realised target on a random share of region-days (news) or region-hours (notices) and missing elsewhere. Detection rates below refer to this sparse, exact planting scheme and are described by the realised effect, because a real content signal with the same realised effect could be easier or harder to detect.
fixed_sentences.A3R6: The exposure, re-admission and matched-support subsets are descriptive and carry no decision class.
fixed_sentences.A3R_BATCH: The new-fit secondary arms use one seed by design, so their three-seed check is not available and their best robustness label is not fully checked.
fixed_sentences.notice_clock_limitation: All 725 notices dated 1 August to 30 September 2026 use the website creation date, a surrogate not verified as the publication time, as their availability clock, whereas the training notices use the official archive clocks; on 65 March-May 2026 notices that carry both clocks the two agree to the second. No pre-specified contrast separates this clock-type change.

methods_sentences: The comparison values are interpretation aids and never enter a decision. For news, the smallest effect size of interest is 3.8% of the reference error, the smallest text-attributed error reduction with a significance test in the cited electricity forecasting work. For notices, the comparison value is 0.5% of the reference error: the equivalence tolerance of the earlier pre-confirmation window-C notice test, used here as a historical-effect reference; that tolerance was set after development results were known and is not an economic indifference threshold.

Every exclusion bound is the conditional one-sided bootstrap bound max(0, −lower endpoint) of a labelled interval: family-adjusted for the primary, combination, absolute-error, pre-dispatch and label-replacement families, and unadjusted for single secondary comparisons; per-contrast 95% intervals of family members appear as intervals only.
Headline intervals are family-adjusted: 97.5% two-sided, that is 1 − 0.05/2 for the 2 pre-specified comparisons of the day-ahead news family; tables also give the per-contrast 95% intervals.
Headline intervals are family-adjusted: 98.3% two-sided, that is 1 − 0.05/3 for the 3 pre-specified comparisons of the market notices family; tables also give the per-contrast 95% intervals.

For notices, the activity-matched reassignment control has no matched key by construction: each notice representation encodes the full saved prefix, so an earlier prefix with the same count contains the same notices, which the donor rule excludes; the notice content-specific label therefore cannot be reached.
The planted-signal check was not run for market notices (no result was available at the time of the fill); the sensitivity of the test pipeline is not documented for this task.
section7_2: Every available pre-specified design sensitivity with a decision rule (the official price-cap re-clip and dropping the first seven notice days) gave the same decision class as the primary readings of the market notices family; independently re-extracted test-period labels and first-chunk encoding were not available.
